name: Why the Map Looks Like That (working name)
promise: A true story about a place or a moment in history so strange it sounds made up, explained in under a minute on a real map.
audience: Curious adults 18-45, English-speaking, who watch Half as Interesting, Knowledgia, RealLifeLore.

benchmarks.study: One astonishing object per episode; premium look.
Deadpan narration; absurd escalation; callback ending.

voice.name: Felix (Fish Audio library, Australian male)
voice.notes: Fish free tier: 50 requests/day across ALL channels. One request per paragraph, cached by hash.

look.texture: cream paper, ink outlines, offset drop shadows, film grain, 12 fps boil

captions.style: Anton, uppercase, 2-5 words per chunk, white with ink outline

safe_zone.note: px at 1080x1920; keep text out of the platform UI (title, buttons, progress bar)

look.notes: Reference implementation: shorts/emu-war/render/emu.js and videos/root-keys/render/lib.js. Maps are Natural Earth only.

series.name: The time a country...
beats: the verdict: a sourced quote or outcome
example_titles: Australia went to war with emus. The emus won.
The time Britain invaded Iceland by accident

series.name: Why does...
beats: hook: the strange fact as a question
the real reason, in 3 steps on the map
example_titles: Why does Canada have a town you can only reach through the US?

series.name: Border weirdness
beats: what life is like there now
example_titles: The Dutch village with houses split in two countries

script.tone: Deadpan, dry, Australian narrator. Never excited; the facts are the joke.
rules: One idea per line. Short sentences. Deadpan: state absurd facts plainly and let the gap carry the joke.
Line one is the hook: the most surprising true sentence in the episode, under the word limit, no preamble.
Spell numbers the way they are spoken ('nineteen thirty-two', 'ten thousand'). Put the digits in the captions.
Every line with a fact, number, name or date cites dossier claim ids. Jokes may not smuggle in new facts.
Estimates and self-reported numbers carry their label on screen (e.g. 'the major's own count').
The last line calls back to the hook or loops into it, so a replay feels intentional.
Use 'gap' (seconds of silence after a line) for comic timing: 0.4-0.6 s before a punchline.

radar: Wikipedia 'On this day' for the next 14 days
Anniversaries (50/75/100 years) in the next 30 days
Border and enclave lists (Wikipedia 'List of enclaves and exclaves')
Current news that touches a place with a strange history
avoid: Active wars and atrocities told as comedy
Claims that exist only in listicles
Topics the channel covered in the last 90 days

preferred: National archives and newspaper archives (e.g. Trove, Chronicling America)
Wikipedia only as a map to its cited sources
sources.notes: Reddit, Quora and social posts may suggest leads but are never cited.

open_decisions: Keep Felix or pick another voice from videos/voice-test/ (user)
